articles.title: 5 DC Comics Stories That Took Beloved Superheroes in Directions Fans Still Haven't Forgotten
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC Comics is responsible for some of the greatest stories in the history of comics. The publisher created the superhero back in 1938 and since then has been refining the concept, all while branching them out into sci-fi, fantasy, horror, romance, slice of life, and basically every other genre you can imagine. They pushed the […]
articles.content:
Over the years, readers have gotten stories that have run the gamut of quality, from amazing and unforgettable to bad and completely forgettable. However, there's another category. There are some stories that have become so infamous they can't be forgotten. Some of them are bad and some of them are just acquired tastes. These five DC stories became unforgettable, but not always for the best reasons.

Countdown to Final Crisis has been maligned for years , but I remember buying it as it came out, being excited for the weekly issues, at least at the beginning. The weekly series came out in 2007, right as 52 ended, leading to the next big DC event, Final Crisis . The story basically takes readers across the DC Multiverse as the Monitors start hunting down multiversal variants and the New Gods begin their cataclysmic final war, with the heroes trying to figure out exactly what is going on.

Countdown to Final Crisis has its moments (I love all the stuff with Karate Kid, for example, and the Jimmy Olsen stuff is fun too), but what has made it so unforgettable is just how much it bungled everything. See, Final Crisis was written by Grant Morrison and at the time, Morrison wasn't really sharing what they were doing with DC editorial. The creators and editors of Countdown basically went rogue and the series doesn't really actually set up Final Crisis at all. Whether you like it or not, it will always be remembered for not even attempting to live up to its title.

The Dark Knight Returns is one of the greatest moments in comic history. Frank Miller's story about a 50-something Batman taking up the cowl again has gone down as one of the books that helped mature the medium and is on numerous best of all-time lists. It has become a seminal moment in comic history and for many fans it has no equals. It also has no sequels for many fans, despite there being several and The Dark Knight Strikes Again is the reason for that. This was the follow-up to the classic and it's become infamous in its own right.

A lot of people will tell you its terrible, but it isn't. It's actually a pretty good DC story set in a dark alternate future. However, it's the sequel to a comic that many consider to be one of the greatest ever and fans had sky expectations. It didn't reach them, so suddenly it's the worst thing ever. The funny thing is a lot of the things that readers complain about were all done in the original as well. It's a story that is remembered for being terrible, but the truth is a bit more complicated than that.

Heroes In Crisis is legitimately hated by many DC fans . The story introduced readers to the concept of Sanctuary, a place where the heroes could go to deal with their own mental issues. When all of the patients there are killed, with only Booster Gold and Harley Quinn surviving, the superhero community mobilizes to figure out who did it, something made more difficult when the existence of Sanctuary is leaked to the press. The story itself is mostly okay, but the reveal of the killer is what makes the book so hated, as it was revealed that Wally West lost control of his powers and accidentally killed everyone, using time travel to commit suicide out of guilt.

Fans immediately rebelled because they loved Wally. However, I think that this story often gets unfairly maligned. While the mystery is kind of blah and it's a little too long for its own good, the concept of Sanctuary is super-interesting and it makes sense that Wally would be as damaged as he was. It's a story that has its problems but that's the case with most comics, it just had the unfortunate honor of doing something no one liked with a character everyone loved.

Convergence is one of the last major New 52 events. It revolves around Brainiac gaining access to the various dead worlds of the multiverse, stealing cities from each of them, and placing them all on one planet, which would become the living being known as Telos, leading to a war between the various heroes and villains. Convergence is a multiverse story that had very little effect on the overall line of DC books and it came at a time when a lot of fans were checked out of the New 52. It's gone down as a failure, but it's actually remembered with some esteem from fans.

While the main book gets its share of negativity, the tie-ins are pretty universally praised, which is rather unique in the pantheon of events. See, each two-issue miniseries took readers to various fan-favorite Earths, including the post- Crisis Earth. That's right, this is the story that brought back the pre- Flashpoint Superman and Lois Lane, all while introducing the world to Jon Kent. So, while this story isn't particularly loved for what it is and had no effect on anything overall, it birthed the best new DC hero in years and has some excellent tie-in books.

Wonder Woman has starred in awesome stories , but not all of them can be great. In fact, some of them can be downright bad, which leads us to 2007's Amazons Attack! . This story spun out of events in Wonder Woman (Vol. 3), when Diana was imprisoned by the US government, leading Hippolyta and the Amazons to attack Man's World in an effort to free her. The rest of the hero community has to step up to stop one of the most potent fighting forces on Earth, but there's more going on than anyone realizes. Honestly, if you just go by that set-up, this story seems like it should be pretty good, but for whatever reason the execution of it was the main problem.

The story was poo-poo'ed by fans and critics alike and it includes some of the most meme-d moments in DC history. The scene that really stands out involves the Amazons using bees to attack the world and Batman saying, “Bees, my god,” as if it was the most dangerous weapon ever. The story did come out in the aftermath of The Wicker Man remake, so it might have been homaging that, but it was just one of many weird moments that made this story unforgettable for all the wrong reasons.

What DC stories do you remember for the wrong reasons? Any you think deserve to be on the list? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Free Nintendo Switch 2 Upgrades Released for 3 Switch Games
articles.summary: Free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades have been released for three Nintendo Switch games. In other words, there are three new Nintendo Switch 2 games that are available for free to those who own the previously released Nintendo Switch versions. It's not incredibly rare for free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades, but it's not common either. To […]
articles.content:
None of the Nintendo Switch 2 games are very expensive, ranging from $15 to $25. If you somehow qualify for all three, though, you are saving a meaningful $65. Meanwhile, some free upgrade paths are restricted to a limited window, but there is no word of that being present here. This trio notably follows a similar free upgrade for a new Sega game .

Herdling is a single-player puzzle game from developer Okomotive and publisher Panic. The former is the studio behind 2018's Far: Lone Sails and 2022's Far: Changing Tides . Upon release, Herdling earned a Metacritic range of 74 to 79. It debuted in 2025.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version, compared to the previous Nintendo Switch version, has enhanced resolution, increased performance, and greater detail, which results in “a smoother and more beautiful experience.”

Herdling , for those who decide to check it out on Nintendo Switch 2, is roughly three to five hours long and normally costs $25.

Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game is a third-person single-player and multiplayer parkour game from developer MLMedia, which debuted with its release in 2025. It has a Metacritic range of 67 to 70.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version increases the game's frame rate from 60 to 120, improves the loading times, adds new community-created content, and adds multiplayer crossplay.

Rooftops & Alleys is about four to ten hours long, though its multiplayer component can bring this range up substantially. It normally costs $25.

A Little to the Left is a cozy puzzle game from developer Max Inferno and publisher Secret Mode. It served as the debut release for the former. Upon release, it earned a Metacritic range of 75 to 77. Of the three games here, it is the most popular, but Herdling is probably the best of the three.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version gives owners higher-resolution graphics, improved frame rates up to 120 fps, faster load times, and adds mouse controls.

A Little to the Left is between four and thirteen hours long, and for this content, Switch 2 users have to fork over $15 to the eShop.

If none of these new releases tickle your Switch 2's fancy, or if you are after something more nostalgic than new, a PS1 exclusive was notably and recently stealth-released on the Switch 2 .

Ricky Ho , one of two composers along with Isabel Latorre, said he toiled over the beginning of the film's signature piece, "Sunset Sonata."

"It's not an easy piece to come up with," Ho said. "It has to be very special, especially the first few notes. Maybe the first two months I write, put aside, take it back, change some notes. “Sunset Sonata” connects the leads of the film as their lives drive them apart. Much of the film involves the Japanese occupation of Singapore.

"It represents their connection, their love together," Ho said. "This piece of music is really important throughout the film."

The epic story also encompasses epic emotions.

"We are melodrama, and we're proud of it," Garcia said. "We need to cry from time to time, and this movie helps you."

Han said he was influenced by the Hong Kong melodramas of the '80s. He saw them with his parents in theaters and understood their catharsis looking back as an adult.

"Animation and especially 2D animation, they have this quality of timelessness," Garcia said. "The movement is stylized. articles.title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys' Bass Singer, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Sterban died Nov. 14 in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the music group announced.
articles.content:
Richard Sterban, the Oak Ridge Boys' bass singer who memorably lent his vocals to their beloved “Elvira” cover, has died. He was 83.

Sterban died Nov. 14 in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the Oak Ridge Boys announced.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus,” Sterban's family said in a statement. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Dawn Greenhalgh, Voice of the Elephant Queen Celeste in 'Babar' Cartoons, Dies at 93 Music Gerry Griffith, Music Executive Who Discovered Whitney Houston, Dies at 87

Born April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, Sterban began singing at six in Sunday school as a soprano. He sang tenor in his seventh-grade glee club, and upon his eighth grade, his voice dropped to bass.

He studied music at Trenton State College (modernly known as the College of New Jersey), and began singing in a gospel quartet where he met Joe Bonsall, his future Oak Ridge Boys bandmate.

While singing part-time, Sterban joined J.D. Sumner and the Stamps, whom Elvis Presley hired to sing behind him. He then sang and recorded with the King of Rock and Roll, and also appeared in the 1972 concert film Elvis on Tour .

Sterban was then offered the opportunity to join the Oak Ridge Boys after the departure of Noel Fox, which he accepted in 1972. Bonsall joined the group one year later, with Duane Allen, William Lee Golden and Sterban already in the group, which carried on as the faces of the band for five decades.

They performed with Johnny Cash, who helped them sign with Columbia Records in 1973, though it was after opening for Roy Clark in 1975 when they met his manger, Jim Halsey, who would later sign with the group. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

They reached success with "Y'all Come Back Saloon,” which reached No. 3 on the country chart in 1977, and led to a string of hits. "I'll Be True to You” became their first No. 1 song, though 1981's “Elvira” would become one of their largest successes.

Originally recorded by Dallas Frazier, the Oak Ridge Boys' version of the track went to No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies and won a Grammy. Sterban's bass refrain was a major touchpoint on the song.

The Oak Ridge Boys went on to also become members of the Grand Ole Opry, the Gospel Music Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Sterban released his memoir From Elvis to Elvira: My Life on Stage , written with Steven Robinson, in 2012.

Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna; his daughters, Lauren (Tyler) and Tori (Michael); his sons, Rich (Chele), Doug, and Chris; his grandchildren, Mali (Zachary), Nikolas, Tyler (Ryann), Madelyn, Alexandra, Rex, Owen, and Charli Grace; and his great-grandchildren, Salem, Asher, and Theo. He was preceded in death by his mother Victoria Sterban, brother Joseph Sterban and grandson Zachary.

articles.title: James Bond Star's Forgotten 29-Year-Old Disaster Movie is Blowing Up on Free Streaming
articles.summary: Courtesy of Universal There are some actors that are part of a huge franchise that make other movies around the same that then get lost to time. That is true of one 1997 disaster movie as not only was its star better known at the time for recently taking on the role of James Bond but had to […]
articles.content:
Dante's Peak is set in the fictional town of Dante's Peak, Washington, as volcanologist Dr. Harry Dalton (Brosnan) investigates seismic activity occurring inside a long-dormant volcano next to the town. Despite Dalton's warnings of imminent disaster, his worries are dismissed until it is too late and the town is engulfed in lava flows and acrid smoke. With the help of the town's mayor (Hamilton) Dalton must lead an evacuation attempt to escape the continued destruction. The film leads into plenty of the usual tropes – Dalton is haunted by the death of his fiancee in a previous eruption, several stubborn residents refusing to evacuate, last minute escapes – and that didn't help make it stand out with reviewers or in its performance in theaters. Although it marginally won the day over Volcano, Dante's Peak ended up being buried in time.

Pierce Brosnan made his debut as James Bond in GoldenEye in 1995 and followed that up with Tomorrow Never Dies in 1997, in between Dante's Peak was a movie that continued to push the Irish actor as an action hero but the execution of the movie and its extortionate budget did not help it stick in the memory for long. That is probably why the film is perfect for free streaming audiences, as a movie with two big star names attached, an action-packed premise and a non-existent legacy meaning most people have forgotten it even exists. When the movie originally hit cinemas with a colossal $116 million budget (one of the highest ever at the time) it was always going to struggle to make enough money from ticket sales alone to break even. With just $178 million worldwide, the final tally made it a flop, especially when compared to Brosnan's Bond adventures.

Dante's Peak did have an advantage of opening two months before Volcano (although that film did not fare any better on its release) after Universal pumped more money into the visual effects teams in order to get their film on screen first. When it debuted the visual effects were one thing that did their job, but for critics everything else was bad from the dialogue to the chemistry even though it is also regarded as one of the most scientifically accurate disaster movies every made. The film scored just 36% with critics and 39% with audiences, who seemed to be on exactly the same page in their assessment that when things were on fire, the film was great, but the rest of the time it was a bit of an ashy mess. However, this is exactly what free streaming is there for, so that people can reacquaint themselves with movies they would not necessarily pay to see again but pass the time when you don't need to pay for a subscription to watch them.

Which movie was better? Dante's Peak or Volcano ? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Boy Meets World’s Danielle Fishel Reveals One Topanga-Related Regret, And I Completely Understand
articles.summary: As a fan, I'm right there with her.
articles.content:
Danielle Fishel charmed audiences for seven seasons while playing the TGIF fan-favorite character , Topanga Lawrence in Boy Meets World . Not only was the character notable for being involved in a TV relationship that defined goals , but Topanga was also loved for being smart and true to herself. While Fishel has taken great pride in her BMW work, she recently mentioned one regret related to her character that, as a fan, I completely sympathize with.

In Fishel, Rider Strong, and Will Friedle’s new book, Book Meets World: The Definitive Inside Story of the Hit Sitcom Boy Meets World (via People ) , she got real about her character's evolution. She explained how she felt about Topanga's trajectory at the time compared to how she feels now:

I get what the Dancing with the Stars contestant is talking about. When Fishel previously spoke about Topanga’s personality shift , she admitted that she didn’t even notice the change at the time. Looking back, it’s true that the show was focusing a lot on Topanga’s evolving look, like in Season 2 when Shawn was staring at her chest or Cory fixated so much on her beauty in Season 3. I truly believe Topanga’s complete change was when she cut her trademark long hair and started to look more like many other woman of the ‘90s.

That would have been great. Fans see a flashback scene in “Resurrection” of when Topanga put lipstick all over her face but, in the later seasons, I would have liked to have seen Fishel's character retain traits of who she was early on.

articles.title: 4 Movies to Get You Ready for Dune: Part Three (Outside the Franchise)
articles.summary: Watching Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) face his first challenges in Dune and claim power in Dune: Part Two was one of the best experiences for fans of the saga and moviegoers in general. But what's the less glamorous side of that journey? Because there is one, and it's what Dune: Part Three is set to […]
articles.content:
However, there's still some time before its December release , so why not check out a few movies that explore these same subjects? We've selected 4 very different features that nevertheless have a lot in common with the story Denis Villeneuve's upcoming film is expected to tell . Whether you still want to better understand Paul's character arc or just get in the mood for the epic conclusion of Dune , this is a good place to start.

Not many people know The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford , as it was never a popular movie, even with its recognizable cast. And those who do know it might find it an unexpected choice to watch before Dune: Part Three . But there's a pretty good reason why it belongs on this list: understanding how a man's image can become more important than who he really is. The story focuses on the final months of Jesse James (Brad Pitt), one of the most notorious outlaws of the Old West, and Robert Ford (Casey Affleck), a young member of his gang who grew up admiring his stories and wants to be part of his inner circle. However, Robert eventually starts seeing Jesse in a very different light.

If you remember the ending of Dune: Part Two , you know that Paul now has to deal with the fact that millions of people no longer see him as Paul, but as the messiah they believe him to be. And that changes things quite a bit, because what his followers expect from him doesn't always match what he actually wants to do. The Assassination of Jesse James explores this same idea by showing how hero worship can get out of hand and how turning someone into a legend can have serious consequences for everyone involved. In Part Three , Paul's choices and everything he does after claiming the throne will play a role in making his situation more complicated . So, if you want a little taste of what's to come, this western is worth watching.

Comparisons between Dune and Star Wars are nothing new , and they've certainly led to plenty of discussions over the years. Still, you can't really separate both franchises when it comes to their Chosen One storylines . Paul and Anakin are two of the most similar characters in sci-fi, and while their journeys take some very different turns, Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith is a great movie to watch if you want a better understanding of where Paul's character arc is really heading. The film follows the final days of the Clone Wars, as Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) takes advantage of the Republic's instability to expand his influence and manipulate Anakin (Hayden Christensen), who is worried about losing Padmé (Natalie Portman). Ultimately, the Jedi becomes Darth Vader .

The connection between these two stories goes well beyond emperors and schemes, as both question what happens when someone who is supposed to represent hope ends up contributing to the creation of an authoritarian regime. Paul isn't Anakin, since he's aware of the dangers of his own rise to power and has a complex relationship with the position he's claimed. Still, both embody the idea that a great savior can become dangerous when people are willing to give up their freedom in exchange for the promise of a better future. Given that Part Three will take a deeper look at everything that happens after Paul takes control of the Imperium, watching Revenge of the Sith is a good way to get into the right mindset.

One of the most iconic war movies ever made , Apocalypse Now is a pick for anyone who wants to experience the more violent side of a story about a powerful leader. Directed by Francis Ford Coppola, the film follows Captain Benjamin Willard (Martin Sheen), who is sent on a mission to find and murder Colonel Walter Kurtz (Marlon Brando), an American military officer who has abandoned his duties and established his own kingdom in a remote part of the jungle during the Vietnam War. The thing is that Kurtz is treated almost like a god by his soldiers, and the closer Willard gets to him, the clearer it is just how much that devotion has warped his worldview. And that's where Paul comes to mind, right? After all, he has also gained a level of power that goes beyond his political position, leading a war that has already spiraled out of control.

The difference is that this movie shows someone who has already reached the extreme end of this process, while Dune hasn't quite gotten there yet — but that's what we'll get to see in Part Three . At the end of the second film, we watched Paul embrace his image as a leader, but that's nothing compared to what happens during his years as Emperor and his role in leading an overwhelming and merciless conflict. And Apocalypse Now is a fantastic opportunity to confront the most disturbing side of this situation: when people follow someone who believes he has the authority to decide everyone else's fate. It also explains why Paul's war shouldn't be seen as a heroic victory , as some viewers might still see the protagonist in a positive way.

The Godfather may be the greatest entry in its trilogy, and one of the best movies ever, but when it comes to Dune , the second film is the bigger reference point . The Godfather Part II captures the kind of situation Paul will face in the next movie tremendously well, since its story isn't really aimed at showing how someone gains power, but rather what happens once they already have it and must figure out how to hold on to it. The iconic movie switches between Vito Corleone's (Robert De Niro) younger years, as he builds the family empire , and the story of his son Michael (Al Pacino), who now has to run the business. But as Michael tries to expand his influence and protect his family, he gets caught up in conspiracies, negotiations, and betrayals that make him paranoid and push him away from those closest to him.

Well, in the first two Dune movies, we've watched Paul try to survive the destruction of his family, earn the Fremen's trust, and claim the throne. But taking control of the Imperium is really just the beginning, isn't it? Now, he has to deal with the consequences of the war he set in motion, the Great Houses that could still threaten his rule, a secret conspiracy working against him from within, and people expecting him to live up to the image of the Lisan al-Gaib. In The Godfather Part II , Michael believes he can control everything and protect his empire, only to realize that holding on to power means destroying what matters most to him. Basically, it's the beginning of his downfall, and Part Three is set to bring that side of Paul's story into full view. Villeneuve didn't call him the Michael Corleone of sci-fi for nothing .

Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18.

The closest I can get without getting on a plane is during Disneyland’s holiday season . Every night, without fail, Main Street U.S.A. and the area in front of “It’s A Small World” become a winter wonderland, and it feels like a fantasy. That is, unless it's raining. I didn’t know before exactly why rain would stop the snow from falling upon Disneyland, but someone just made the reason quite evident.

“Disneyland’s Wintertime Enchantment” makes snowfall in Southern California possible every night at 7:30 p.m. and 8:30 p.m. However, don’t count on it if it’s raining. And FYI, there’s a lot of it coming this week after some notable flooding at Disneyland last month . Here’s why:

A post shared by Molly Evans (@happilyevansafterall)

Now, I hate to ruin the magic, but Disneyland snow isn’t actually snow. It’s something that’s been named "snoap" by fans, because it’s practically soap disguised as snow. It's dispersed by hidden rooftop machines.

According to the Los Angeles Times , Disneyland’s snow is made up of 98% water mixed with a non-hazardous, proprietary surfactant (soap) blend. On any other day, the “snow” evaporates shortly after landing somewhere and leaves no trace on guests or around the park. However, when too much water mixes with it, you get a very soapy (and gross) ground!

As you can see in the Instagram post, when the “snoap” and rain happen at the same time, it creates a major slip hazard for the guests. Therefore, it is usually canceled on rainy days. In this recent instance, the guest reports that snow was accidentally turned on at 10:30 p.m., causing an issue everywhere in the park where snow fell.

The firework show will have to be canceled during active rain, heavy cloud cover or high winds, but the projections at “It’s A Small World” will typically still run.

The “It’s A Small World” ride also has a special holiday version if you’re not into that song . The World of Color - Season of Light over at California Adventure can also usually hold up unless rain is paired with severe wind or lightning. And you can meet Santa Claus at Mickey’s Toontown Trolley Barn, which is located indoors.

One of my personal favorite holiday traditions is the A Christmas Fantasy Parade. I just love seeing all the characters in their Christmas-themed outfits, too. Over at DCA, there’s also a holiday event called “Guardians of the Galaxy: Awesome Dance Off!” debuting at Avengers Campus. Disneyland’s holiday-themed entertainment runs until January 6 this year, so there’s plenty of time to enjoy this special time of year.

If you’re not able to make it to Disneyland right now, it’s also a good time to check out the 2026 Christmas movie schedule . A ton are available to stream with a Disney+ subscription !

articles.content:
As evidenced by the latest Toy Story film, technology is here to stay in toys and beyond.

For producer Lindsey Collins , whose credits also include Disney / Pixar ‘s A Bug's Life , Ratatouille , Finding Nemo and Turning Red , the key is balancing not overdeveloping the looks of animations in the films with moving them forward to suit advancements humanity has made and better capture certain details.

"[We] try to keep it so we're not evolving it so fast or so much that people are like, ‘This doesn't feel like the Toy Story I recognize or I know,' but also make sure that we're keeping it so that we're taking advantage of all the things we can do," Collins said on a panel at Deadline's Contenders Film Los Angeles event. "The technology just lets us do anything now. At the time, it was so restricted, like no hair or fur on the dog, or you couldn't have you have tight clothing on everybody. One of the things that we're really proud of is the character Blaze, who we all love, who's the friend that ultimately comes as the gift at the end of the film. There was a version of the film's ending where star character Jessie (voiced by Joan Cusack) meets an older version of her previous owner, Emily.

"Because it was Jessie's story, we knew we wanted her to reckon with the past with Emily, and there was a version at one point where she actually meets Emily, all grown up and old, and and we were like, “That's a trip. OK, does that feel satisfying?' As an audience, there was a lot of conversation around what's going to be the satisfying gift for Jesse at the end," Collins said. "Is it seeing Emily? Is it kind of understanding, getting the chance to kind of play with her again? These toys are like vampires; they don't age. The rest of the world ages around them. articles.title: Superman Became the Flash in One of These Bizarre Silver Age Stories, and That's Just the Beginning
articles.summary: When you've been around for as long as Superman, your adventures are bound to get a bit strange. We've read plenty of issues where ol' red and blue has punched his way out of trouble, struggled with his dual life, joined the Justice League, and even returned from the dead. While those are all interesting […]
articles.content:
While they aren't landmark issues by any measure, they are definitely on the weirder side. For instance, in Action Comics #211 , Daily Planet chief Perry White asks Superman to travel to different parts of the world and perform stunts for the local editions of the newspaper. It seems crime was taking a break that day, as Supes readily agreed to go on this strange quest. Issue #289 features Supergirl trying to set up her cousin with different people, including Helen of Troy from the past, and Saturn Girl from the 30th century, and another alien on Earth. When all that fails, there's an awkward moment where they consider dating each other but decided that a relationship between first-cousins would be weird. Thank Rao.

Things only get stranger from there. You've heard of Krypto the Super Dog, but did you know there was also a Super Horse? Issues #292 and #293 featured the first appearance of the superpowered stallion, but it's not as simple as just being a horse from Krypton. It turns out the horse was originally a centaur from ancient Greece, and was tricked with a potion that turned him fully into a horse. As compensation, the sorceress Circe blessed Comet with super strength and invulnerability, but was eventually exiled to the stars. He was finally only able to escape when Supergirl's rocket from Krypton passed by. The two then formed a temporary alliance to fight off a group of aliens. I bet you've never heard of this one.

To round it off, Adventure Comics #314 , features Superman becoming The Flash, and even other members of the League. The two have always been compared when it comes to speed, but this issue literally put Supes into the Flash's lightening themed shoes. It starts with The Justice League finding a lost recording of Superman's father Jor-El running simulations of where he could send his infant son when Krypton eventually comes to an end. One of the planets would involve Superman retaining his trademark powers, but would be the size of an ‘Atom', compared to the native species. Another is a water-based world, which would bestow him with the same powers as Aquaman. Are you sensing a theme here? The next two planets feature a clear red sun and an eclipsed red sun, with the simulations showing him turning into Green Arrow and Batman respectfully. However, the most interesting of the lot is the planet Gangor, where Kal-El would develop super speed. However, with no one to train him, the simulations revealed that he could literally run right off the planet. Thankfully, Jor-El settled on Earth. Superman clearly went on some wild, and even questionable adventures in the '60s, and this collection has captured them all for one lucky collector.

What according to you is the most bizarre adventure Superman has ever gone on? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Prolific director, screenwriter and producer Peter Farrelly reflected on some of his most famous films Saturday at Deadline's Contenders Film Los Angeles event.

Contenders Hall of Fame honoree Farrelly talked with Deadline's Mike Fleming Jr about his most recent film I Play Rocky and the process of bringing it to the screen. Earlier, Farrelly had appeared on the film's panel with star Anthony Ippolito, who plays Sylvester Stallone in the film, and talked about the uphill battle to making the crowd-pleasing underdog tale.

Farrelly revealed that it was his daughter's ex-boyfriend who first read the script and told Farrelly it “was the best script he had ever read.” Farrelly agreed and pushed forward with the film, noting it was imperative that he had Stallone's approval on the script, which came quickly. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He also shared his own “Rocky” moment: “The bravest thing I ever did in my life was decide to write when I was in my mid-20s,” he said.

Farrelly also talked about his years and years of getting turned down for scripts and having to push through the rejection and not give up. As for 1994's Dumb & Dumber , “We wrote that script five years before it got made, and it was the exact same script,” he shared. “Every studio passed, every actor passed.” He acknowledged that he changed the title to A Power Tool Is Not a Toy and “everyone started reading it.” It was the eventual film's star Jim Carrey who told him Dumb & Dumber is the title, “so we went back to that,” he said.

“You've got to believe,, that they're wrong and you're right,” he said regarding the rejections. “You know, year after year getting turned down, it's hard. You just gotta stick out and hope that you're right.”

One of the most memorable and hilarious scenes in Farrelly's films was in There's Something About Mary and Cameron Diaz's “hair gel.” “I realized we were going to have to go to R [in that film] because we were right on the PG-13 line.

“There's two things that the studio didn't want was the zipper joke in the beginning and the hair gel thing of course, and we understood that, especially the hair gel.” But of course, the hair gel stayed in and the rest is history.

articles.content:
Chris Pratt “would love” to make a fourth Guardians of the Galaxy movie if James Gunn wanted to revisit the Marvel film franchise after his exit from DC Studios .

"That would be awesome," Pratt told MovieZine when asked about the potential of a fourth film. "I love working with James [Gunn]. He's the man. “So all I'll say is I love James. articles.content:
I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was "the winner…" followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

No, Miss American Idol did not abandon her feud with the Brooklyn bird to capitalize on her newfound appreciation for AI . But as I approached the Mayan Theater in Downtown Los Angeles on a sunny afternoon to check in for Friday's inaugural "AI Music Awards," powered by the " Sonic Intelligence Academy " or "SIQA," I wondered if her voice was so strong as to echo through the nearly century-old theater-turned-nightclub's walls. To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA's "Verified Registry," which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a "human + AI hybrid").

Registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 categories up for consideration — everything from "AI Song of the Year" to "Best AI Pop Song" to "Best AI Comedic Song" — and then vote on the winners. One of those nominees was Xania Monet, the AI persona of Telisha "Nikki" Jones, who a day earlier won the AI Album of the Year category at SIQA's inaugural summit and who would eventually go on to win both artist and song of the year, three out of four of the awards' top categories. The Sonic Intelligence Academy is the brainchild of software engineer Timirah "TJ" James and her sister Mia James. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry's aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

It's a noble, if surprising, decision to embrace its role as counterculture when AI artists continue to pursue a Billboard charting position. Some of its methods are a little overt, perhaps intentionally: After some in the industry spurned the idea of AI-generated music charting on Billboard's industry-standard charts, the group used a week in January ahead of the Grammys to launch its own charts exclusively for AI music. The Mayan is a 12-minute walk from the Crypto.com Arena, the Grammys' longtime home.

The moves are not subtle, but subtlety is not the organization's goal. The group and awards' existence alone reflects those in the AI music space trying to move past the thorny legal questions surrounding AI music, which have led to lawsuits by artists and record labels against generators like Suno and Udio over copyright infringement, and into a realm of relevance within the genres they're trying to embody.

It is, in a word, new, and new things mean kinks to work out.

The first kink I noticed was when, as I arrived 30 minutes before the red carpet was set to begin, the doors to the venue were locked. I had to pull on each door before someone opened one, which led me to the check-in stand (bypassing any form of security, which didn't seem to exist). I entered the foyer and arrived at the makeshift red carpet, where about 12, mostly independent media ventures set up cameras to interview the various nominees, presenters, and VIPs who'd grace the roughly 7-foot-long red carpet in front of one of the two step-and-repeat backdrops. A spokesperson told me 29 media outlets had signed up to cover the event, but that some couldn't make it because of the sudden flight ground-stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration around 12:30 p.m. PT. Whether human or AI, aviation afflictions come for us all. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The guests gracing the red carpet were not screens rolled out displaying AI avatars, contrary to a reasonable assumption. Instead, the human creators behind the digital faces strutted the carpet in their Sunday best, treating the night less as music's biggest night and more as the biggest night for their music. Sequined dresses and colorful blazers strolled through, stopping to speak with outlets like Reuters to the fiery red mohawk-sporting, sequin-wearing host of "The Iconic Punk Oz" Oz Powers to, tucked against a wall and steps from the red carpet, an effective AI red carpet correspondent housed inside a tall, white faux-stone vessel. The contraption was developed by the event's top sponsor, Deepgram, an AI startup specializing in text-to-speech agents.

The device, which knew the artists and pressed them about the event, struck in me a slight fear about whether people might opt for robot reporters instead of humans, though that fear subsided when I realized this device could not appear on the red carpet because it could not move. The creators seemed more eager to speak to the physical reporters anyway, with some of them emphasizing the human elements of their AI work. Fredro Starr, one half of the rap group Onyx, spent much of the carpet touting the human vocals that made up his AI-beat-laden record "It All Started in Brooklyn," which he claimed was the first AI album on vinyl.

"You can't replace [humans]," Starr told me, using the carpet to debut his new moniker, "Mad AI." "The feeling that you get was what we bring with the spirit of hip-hop. So vocally, you can hear that, but the AI just took it to another level."

Inside the theater, SIQA tried to bring a party-like feel to the function. A bar at the back of the venue —at a charge — kept well drinks flowing, and the bar top was littered with copies of a sponsored version of the newspaper "Rolling Out" featuring interviews with many of the nominees and James, the SIQA founder. One of those featured, Xania Monet founder Jones, sparked a wave of controversy last year when some of her Monet songs hit some of Billboard's genre charts, leading to an interview with CBS's Gayle King and to Kehlani slamming a $3 million record deal Jones received. As she waited for a drink by the bar ahead of the event's start, Jones told me she wasn't worried about the AI of it all overshadowing the pursuit of legitimacy within the greater music industry. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"AI is just a tool," she said. "It just emphasizes what we do. I just feel like we should all be one."

But despite that lofty goal, the kinks kept rearing their heads.

The event started about 30 minutes past its 6:15 p.m. start time, skipping a planned opening video montage for a dance break performed and choreographed by actor Giovanni Wilson with eight dancers to a seemingly AI-produced song that described — in literal terms — how we were at the inaugural AI music awards. The delay forced the show to skip introducing the nominees for the first half of the awards and instead have presenters just state the winner, robbing some attendees of hearing their names called for what felt like one of their biggest achievements.

The event was hosted by Wilson and podcast host Lana Hout, one half of the podcasting duo the "AI Chicks," with a three-member house band of real people playing guitar, bass, keys and drums, soundtracking much of the night. The two hosts shared the only two microphones apparently available throughout the night, with a teleprompter loaded with the Claude-generated run-of-show, but they often seemed lost about what category, presenter, performance or commercial break was next.

At one point, Hout and Wilson were confused over whether they would cut to commercial or bring out the two presenters for best AI country artist. They then brought out the two country award presenters, only for Hout to walk back out mid-introduction to interrupt and say that, actually, they would go to commercial break. The award was eventually presented 13 minutes later with a different presenter.

Oftentimes, the use of AI seemed to hover over some of the technical hiccups. Deepgram was meant to power an AI voice that introduced the night's presenters and nominees, but it often didn't work and, when it did, talked over many of the presenters. Deepgram also had a commercial that played throughout the evening, but it would sometimes play at random moments even when a commercial break wasn't called. The Deepgram team sat on the couch to my left, and when I looked over to see their reaction to the madness, one member had her head in her hands.

Early in the night, Wilson tried to introduce a trailer for his latest acting gig, the Terrance Howard-led film "A Good Hand Wasted" that he said used AI to help finish the project, but none of Wilson's cues seemed to get it to play. Once it finally did, the screen only played a portion of the trailer before Howard's face even appeared. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"So, ugh," he said, before raising his hand to summon the audience's applause.

The teleprompter was not much help, often shifting rapidly as presenters were speaking. The chaos led Wilson, who spent much of the night trying to maintain some decorum throughout the frustration, to joke they were "dealing with a prompter that has Tourette's."

The commercials for the event featured Deepgram and a new social network called "Trinity Social," with the latter's AI-generated ad featuring a persona wearing a necklace of the Rockstar Games logo encouraging a stadium full of generated people to sign up for the app. A Rockstar spokesperson did not respond to an immediate request for comment on whether it authorized the logo, though if it did not, the ad would represent the latest in AI content lifting copyrighted material without permission, all at an event celebrating a use of AI that has rankled the music industry over similar concerns.

Some of the greatest energy came from the evening's nearly 10 performances, all of which made the cut despite the event running nearly 40 minutes behind schedule the entire night.

There had been some speculation over how, exactly, songs produced with AI and presented by AI avatars would play on stage. It turns out, through the power of lip-syncing and acting. Some acts, like country artist Ava Bentley and R&B artist EJ Rogers, lip-synced their entire performance, while others relied on hired performers who did even that for them. For "Chaisen Hale," a project that features a video of an AI-generated boy with AI-generated vocals, a human lookalike singer named John Victor, 14, was brought out to lip-sync to the track. Attendees — including one duo, for some reason, dressed as Frankenstein and his bride — were generally riveted.

Nearly all of the performances were backed by the live band and dancers, who were provided to the artists for free by SIQA. Many who produce music with AI say they did so because they could not afford the studio musicians and resources required to bring their tracks to life, which made the reliance on the house band feel more like an opportunity to live out their dreams without the cost often paid by traditional artists who hire such musicians to produce their work. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Some of the only actual live vocals came from a rapper named GodFellow and Grammy-winning singers Eric Bellinger and Candace Wakefield, the latter of whom made a point to note the "hiccups" throughout the night and that she was singing live as she performed a song by AI artist "Aria Blue." The performances captured much of what remained in the crowd, which grew smaller and smaller as the night progressed.

James, the SIQA founder, acknowledged the "technical difficulties" ahead of presenting Jones with her awards, but she promised those would be resolved ahead of next year's ceremony.

"Because there will be a next year because this is the new music industry," she told the crowd around 9:45 p.m., just as it was hitting its hard end time. "SIQA has created the infrastructure for that industry and for all the artists coming up in that industry."

And for many of the people in the room, that's all they wanted. One artist, Sheena Taylor, accepted her award for best AI gospel song for a track called "I Denounce You, Satan," by acknowledging the intense traumas she endured that led to a religious discovery. Another artist named Ramona Höffel, a 56-year-old woman who spends her days helping disabled people, flew in from Switzerland to represent her AI persona "Vireya" on her first-ever red carpet. (When I addressed her by her given name, she snapped at me.)

"I have a lot of ideas and wishes, and for a long time I paint, then I write, and that's not enough," she said, visibly nervous to be the first person to walk the red carpet. "The music gives me room to all this bring outside of my brain."

I thought about Höffel's words as I left the venue just after 10 p.m., well past the event's scheduled 9:30 end, and into the downtown rain. To my right was a line forming to get into the venue for "Club 2010s" night , now delayed due to the prolonged awards show. It's unclear whether AI music will generate an enduring monoculture in the way the music from the 2010s has, particularly as the larger music industry has mostly ostracized it. But it's left people like Höffel feeling stronger, which is all someone like 2011 chart-topper Kelly Clarkson could ask for.

articles.title: New Persona 6 Update Points to Trailer Coming Soon
articles.summary: A new Persona 6 update has surfaced online, signaling that a trailer is coming soon. The Persona 5 follow-up was first announced by Atlus back in June of this year after many years of rumors. Then, in September, just two months ago, Atlus announced the long-awaited RPG is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in addition […]
articles.content:
Atlus recently updated the Persona 6 domain. In fact, it made a very specific update that comes with precedent. As a user on the Persona 6 Reddit notes , the Persona 6 domain in question used a Wildcard Certificate, which in turn enables Atlus to make massive website changes in the back end without said changes going live. More than this, this exact thing happened with Persona 4 Revival . A month later, it received its first major trailer. The timing of this is also noteworthy. A month from now is The Game Awards, a likely destination for such a reveal.

The stars appear to be alligning for a Persona 6 reveal soon, as the first trailer was a mere announcement teaser trailer. It didn't actually reveal the game. What about a release date, though?

Between reveal and release, there were nearly three years between the reveal and release of Persona 5 . Atlus has suggested in the past it doesn't want to repeat this large gap again, though. Persona 5 Roya l, meanwhile, had a 6-month gap. Persona 3 Reload had an 8 month gap. And then Persona 4 Revival has about a 1-year and 8-month gap. It's hard to take these numbers and apply them to Persona 6 for various reasons. In the absence of a compelling pattern, the most recent release is the best example to look at, which is Persona 4 Revival . If Persona 6 follows in these footsteps, it will be fall or holiday 2027.

All of that said, take everything here with a grain of salt. The domain update is real, but we can't conclusively say it means one thing or another. The speculation isn't wild. It's very reasonable, but it is still speculation.

At the moment of publishing, Atlus has commented on nothing above, and we do not expect this to change for a plethora of reasons. If it does, though, we will update the accordingly.

Persona 6 is in active development for Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X. There is currently no word of a release date or when the next official update will arrive.

When the script for the uniquely sonic-minded Tuner made its way to sound designer Johnnie Bunn, he was surprised to discover that the plot hinges on hyperacusis, the acute sensitivity to sound that leads the movie's lead character make the shift from piano tuner to safecracker.

"I was like, “Oh my goodness – I've had this condition,'" Burn revealed at Deadline's Contenders Los Angeles event Saturday. "In my late teens, I witnessed an explosion, and immediately I was 100% deaf. At the time, I went into my bedroom and played Public Enemy, and I could feel the speakers and I was like, ‘I can't hear anything, but I can [feel the sound]' So it was horrifying. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Literally about 20 minutes later, my hearing came back, but for about four months I had this," Burn continued. "So I was well aware of what it is, and it's not the big sounds that you're seeing here, particularly in the movie.

articles.title: It’s Not Too Late for Indiana Jones’ Most Underused Character to Take Over the Franchise
articles.summary: In the world of franchise filmmaking, Indiana Jones is starting to feel like a bit of an anomaly. While every other film series is being rebooted or reimagined, Indy remains relatively steadfast in its commitment to the original vision. In 1981’s Raiders of the Lost Ark, director Steven Spielberg and star Harrison Ford created an […]
articles.content:
Of course, two more sequels followed: 2008’s Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull and 2023’s Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny . Both films seemed intent on ending the franchise on its own terms, with the latter featuring James Mangold ( Logan ) replacing Spielberg in the director’s chair. But now it seems like Ford’s tenure leading what was once among the top movie franchises of all time is over. This begs the question: what is the future of the Indiana Jones franchise? With such a valuable franchise in hand, Disney isn’t likely to leave it dormant for good. As it turns out, the answer has actually been quietly waiting in the wings for decades.

Fans at the time may have balked at how different 1984’s Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom was from its predecessor. Not only was the film so dark that it was instrumental in creating the PG-13 rating, but it also served as a prequel to Raiders of the Lost Ark before George Lucas’ Star Wars saga cemented the term in the pop-culture vernacular. Reportedly, the intention was to make the films more of an anthology of standalone Indy adventures . However, with the more recent sequels harkening back to the series’ history, that initial goal appears to be, well, ancient history. So rather than recasting another actor as Indiana Jones, the smart move would be to shift the franchise’s focus over to another hero who already has a devoted fanbase.

Temple of Doom introduces moviegoers to a young boy named Short Round , who apparently had joined Indy on multiple adventures prior to the events of the film. He serves not only as Indy’s sidekick but is presented as something of a protégé. As played by Ke Huy Quan in his first-ever film role, the character brings a very different energy to the story and is widely beloved by fans. When Indy is under Mola Ram’s trance, Short Round breaks him out of it, declaring the hero his best friend. The unlikely friendship between these two is the emotional core of Temple of Doom . And now is the perfect time to bring Quan back to lead a new film.

Quan famously stepped away from acting in the early 1990s after being dissatisfied with the roles out there. If he had been working when Kingdom of the Crystal Skull was in production, it’s easy to imagine an alternate version of that film where Short Round returns and is set up as the next-generation hero. Instead, that film introduced Shia LaBeouf’s Mutt Williams, a character who failed to connect with audiences. Despite being revealed as Indy’s son with Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), he is unceremoniously killed off-screen by the time Dial of Destiny begins. So the path toward re-introducing a new successor to the franchise is already clear.

Of course, now Quan is an Oscar winner for his comeback performance in Everything Everywhere All At Once . And moreover, he has already taken his first leap toward a potential run as an action hero. Granted, 2025’s Love Hurts was a box office misfire, but Quan’s charisma and action prowess continue to make anything he’s in that much better. If Disney wants the Indiana Jones franchise to continue, it needs to move past Ford’s iconic performance. A simple recast wouldn’t work, as the short-lived TV series The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles proved in the 1990s. But building a new adventure around Quan’s Short Round — especially with Ford in a baton-passing supporting role a la Creed — could be the series’ best bet of staying relevant.

Do you want to see Quan back in his iconic New York Giants cap as Short Round for a new adventure set in the world of the previous Indiana Jones films? Let us know in the comments below!

Russell Brand has been at the center of a legal situation, and it recently ended with him being sentenced to years in prison. (This came several years after five women made allegations against Brand – which he denied – as part of an investigation conducted by the Sunday Times and Channel 4’s Dispatches.) Brand’s four-week trial ended with him being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. His aforementioned sentence ultimately came down on November 9.

It was in September 2024 that Combs was arrested in New York shortly after his homes in California and Florida were raided as part of a federal investigation. articles.title: Charlie Cox Responds to MCU Future & If Daredevil Will Be Recast
articles.summary: It's been known for quite some time now that Daredevil: Born Again will be ending after its upcoming third season, which is set to air in 2027. Most fans assumed this would be the end for certain characters, but actor Vincent D'Onofrio, who plays Kingpin, didn't share that view. He even went so far as […]
articles.content:
At the Welcome to the Multiverse convention in Paris, France, Cox took the stage to talk about his run as Daredevil and answer a few questions. The long-rumored David Fincher-directed standalone Daredevil project was mentioned, and Cox admitted that the role would likely be recast if that project were to move forward. This didn't stop the internet from immediately running wild with rumors, implying that Marvel had long had plans to replace Cox as the masked hero, or that they were going to reboot the series without him in an attempt to correct what the Feige brothers thought were mistakes within the MCU.

And while it doesn't seem that a recast is actually in the cards, and Fincher has famously passed on superhero movies throughout the entirety of his career, people quickly made their opinions about the idea known. One fan said on X , “He's this generation's Daredevil; get him in the Movies now! The actor and character portrayal deserve it! Team him up with Spider-Man in his next movie AND throw him in the final battle of Secret Wars , where they'll probably try to outdo Endgame's final battle.” Another agreed, following up with, “Please, Marvel Studios, no. Cox is a great Daredevil, and there's still so much more we can do…” And more than a handful of fans are incensed by the clickbait nature of the tweets, which pushed a story that wasn't even close to what was actually happening.

As for what's actually coming next for Daredevil and Co., it's anyone's guess. The series is set to wrap next year, with Brad Winderbaum, Marvel Television’s big boss, saying, “The plan was always to culminate at 3, because the way we’re looking at it, the original series is 3 seasons, Born Again is 3 seasons. They’re kind of like trade paperbacks or collections that you can slot into your shelves, like these are two 3-volume sets, and then we will take a breath and figure out what’s next for the character.” But fans are right about one thing: it's long past time that we got Matt Murdock and the rest of the crew on the big screen.

articles.summary: This would've been a sweet way to bring him back.
articles.content:
Robert Downey Jr. is making his long-awaited return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in a little over a month but, this time, he won’t be playing Tony Stark (a.k.a. Iron Man). The Oscar-winning actor will, instead, play the villainous Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday . Joe and Anthony Russo’s superhero team-up flick will mark Downey’s first MCU outing in over seven years (and, boy, did that time fly). That aside, though, I was surprised to find that the star could’ve reappeared in the sprawling franchise a bit sooner.

Although I enjoyed VisionQuest (as many critics did as well), I would’ve appreciated the scene Matalas described (on X ). The show reveals that Tony isn’t the actual creator of the A.I. technology responsible for birthing J.A.R.V.I.S., E.D.I.T.H. and co from the majority of Markridge Biotech’s co-founders. It’s an intriguing reveal and one that adds a little wrinkle to MCU lore. It sounds like even Matalas would’ve relished the moment as well, but he also brought up a fair point:

The shadow of the highly quotable Tony Stark still looms large over the MCU, though, in more than a few ways. Not only are his A.I. creations still roaming the Earth (and interwebs), but his protégé, Peter Parker, is also carrying on his work in some ways. And, while Stark may not have mentored Riri Williams , she’s followed in his metal footsteps by becoming Ironheart. Overall, I can imagine that many will continue to hold Tony’s memory close, especially during the ordeal that’ll likely unfold in Marvel’s latest 2026 movie schedule entry.

articles.title: The Biggest Fantasy Series of the Decade Is Ruling Streaming with Its Long-Awaited New Season
articles.summary: Courtesy of Prime Video While it is hard for some fantasy TV shows to usually get beyond one or two seasons thanks to the high budgets and struggle to get audiences to invest, there have been several exceptions to the rule. One of these has now released the first four episodes of its third season on Prime Video, and […]
articles.content:
The Rings of Power debuted on Prime Video in 2022 with the first season of a proposed five-season plan that would cost somewhere in the region of $1 billion when all is said and done. The show focuses on events that took place during the second age of Middle Earth, 1000s of years before The Lord of the Rings , but the timeline for the show has been truncated a little to seemingly allow it to incorporate characters and moments that would otherwise not happen until much later. This is just one gripe that some die-hard Tolkien enthusiasts have vocally expressed on social media and via review-bombing of the series over the last several years. However, for the vast majority, The Rings of Power has been a welcome addition to the franchise and one that brings a truly cinematic series to television like never before.

The first season of The Rings of Power spent a lot of its time establishing this slightly altered version of Tolkien's world, while the second focused on the rising power of Sauron and his ability to manipulate those around him into doing his bidding while frequently crossing paths with the elf Galadriel. In Season 3, viewers will finally see Sauron creating the most powerful item in the franchise , the One Ring. To do this, he must seek out unlikely help from one of The Lord of the Rings ‘ most fearsome and stunning creatures, the Balrog, who will actually speak – in the voice of Simon Pegg – for the first time ever on screen. Meanwhile, Gandalf has found his identity and is on his own journey which plays out in parallel to that of Sauron's quest for power.

The opening four episodes have received the usual mix of high praise and continued complaints for not following Tolkien's text on the time period to the letter. In the main, the series has continued to receive positive reviews from critics, with the Rotten Tomatoes score holding 81% in line with previous seasons, while the audience score sits on 68%. Yet, it is clear from the reviews that if you step back from the belief that every adaptation of an existing book series should not make any changes and only adapt it as it was written, then you will find this is the best and most focused season of The Rings of Power so far, and one of the best, most polished fantasy series to ever be brought to TV. As the series' position in the chart has proven yet again, the number of people jumping back into the show and sticking with it far outweigh those with a negative opinion of it.

Is The Rings of Power delivering one of the best shows on TV? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

Tenzing director Jennifer Peedom 's journey to bring the story of Tenzing Norgay, the too-often-forgotten Sherpa who scaled Mount Everest alongside the more credited Sir Edmund Hillary, was akin to scaling an epic mountain in its own right. And like the original 1953 feat, she achieved it with a vital assist from Norgay himself.

"My career began as an aspiring documentary filmmaker, and the jobs that helped me get into documentary filmmaking were camera-operating jobs, which happened to be on Everest," Peedom said during a panel for the film at Deadline's Contenders Los Angeles event Saturday. "I worked as a climbing camera operator on Everest expeditions, and through that I met many Sherpas, and I worked with the same team of Sherpas for many years. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I then made a feature documentary about 10 years after my first trip there that followed an Everest expedition from the Sherpa's point of view, really to highlight the disproportionate risks that Sherpas take in helping foreigners achieve their dreams," Peedom added, recalling her acclaimed 2015 film Sherpa . "It was the aftermath of that film that led to the idea of making this film, just a recognition that this story hadn't been told."

Through the making of Sherpa , Peedom had met and become friendly with Norgay's children, which led to a pivotal moment: "Norgay came to the world premiere of Sherpa , which happened to be in Sydney," the Australian filmmaker said. "And I brought him out onstage after, and the whole audience stood to their feet. And it kind of struck me that there was just this hunger to this idea that they were touching greatness."

She recalled: "There was something spiritual about that man and about Tenzing's achievement. And it was really clear to, I think, both of us that the audience were hungry for this story. And it was really after that, that we kind of came at the idea at the same time because I had thought about making this film. I was nervous to ask him, and then he asked me and we both kind of came at the idea, really, together."

"[ Tenzing ] is very much a story about Tenzing's spiritual relationship to the mountain that he calls Chomolungma," Peedom noted. "It's also a story about family and identity and belonging and grief and an understanding of what it was that was driving Tenzing up that mountain."

articles.title: I’ve Been Wondering If Tangled 2 Will Happen Even With The Live-Action Remake. Someone Asked An Exec
articles.summary: Will a sequel ever get out of its tower?
articles.content:
In an age of prequels, sequels and reboots, I kind of expect most successful films to get at least one of those things. Weirdly, Tangled hasn’t. Yes, it is getting a live-action adaptation, and there was the animated series Rapunzel’s Tangled Adventure . However, it has not gotten an animated sequel to go along with the 2010 hit. Now, someone asked a Disney exec if there are any plans to ever make a Tangled 2 .

While Bush didn’t confirm or deny whether there have been talks about a Tangled sequel, it does seem like, to get one made, it would need to have a director leading the charge who cares deeply about it and a story that has to be seen on the big screen. Makes sense to me. I wouldn’t want to see a sequel to one of the best princess movies ever if it didn’t have those two things either.

Overall, it sounds like the bar is very high for a Tangled sequel (as it should be), and maybe that’s why we’ve never seen one. However, considering we’ve gotten two Frozens and now they’ve gotten a third one off the ground , I will never totally give up on Tangled 2 .

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Fans Slam "Pathetic" Downgrade in Switch 2 Remake
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake on Nintendo Switch 2 has a bizarre downgrade compared to the N64 original, which has left some fans very frustrated. While the new remake is a fairly faithful one, it's not a one-for-one remake. There are changes, and some cut content as well. Most of these changes […]
articles.content:
Those who played the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64 will know it gave players three manual save slots. The new Nintendo Switch 2 remake only gives players one manual save slot, which some players have found out the hard way after starting new playthroughs and then discovering their previous files gone. This led to one player losing their 100% playthrough .

Now, when you start a new playthrough, the game warns you that your previous auto-save data will be overwritten. What it doesn't make clear is that, unlike the original, you aren't getting manual save slots.

There is a workaround to this problem, and it's having more than one account. This is the only way to effectively have multiple save slots. As for why Nintendo limits players to one manual save slot, we have no idea, but players aren't happy about it.

“This is my major gripe, and it would have been so easy to implement that the fact they didn't baffles me. I hope they add multiple save slots,” reads one of the top comments on the aforementioned Reddit post about this matter. A second fan adds, “That’s absolutely pathetic if true.”

It's also worth noting you can do a second playthrough on the same profile and not lose your original save if you play the second only using auto saves. This is obviously not ideal, though. Further, your autosaves will be overwritten if you boot back into your manual save and play a bit.

While this is frustrating for players, it's not a huge surprise. It's a surprise based on the original, but this has been the design choice of Nintendo with the series for a while. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom both work the same way. We know DLC is coming , so perhaps this problem will be remedied then, but you never can count on anything with Nintendo.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is available on Nintendo Switch 2, and the Nintendo Switch 2 only, for $70. Right now, it is the highest-rated game of 2026.

articles.title: 5 Most Powerful Dragon Ball Super Characters Goku Can’t Defeat
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Warning: This article contains spoilers from the Dragon Ball Super manga! Dragon Ball Super was released as a sequel to the main story, and it expanded the world-building by introducing the parallel universes. As the world became larger, more characters were introduced, each with their own set of powers and abilities. Two decades after concluding […]
articles.content:
However, just when things seemed calm, the God of Destruction named Beerus , known to be the most powerful deity in the universe, awakened from his slumber. Not long after awakening, he began searching for a legendary Super Saiyan God he saw in a prophetic dream. Since Beerus’ thrilling fight with Goku, the manga has featured one adventure after another as Goku and the Z Fighters continue to become more powerful. Over the years, Goku has reached new heights of power that he never thought were possible. Even so, he still can't defeat these five extraordinarily powerful characters.

Beerus was the first opponent of Goku introduced in Dragon Ball Super , and even now, hardly any characters can beat him. While initially an antagonist of the Battle of Gods Arc, it didn't take long for him to join Goku's side since what he needed was a worthy rival. During the Battle of Gods Arc, Goku borrowed the powers of his fellow Saiyans and awakened a legendary form called the Super Saiyan God. However, even after Goku used up all of his newfound powers, Beerus still only had to use a fraction of his powers to easily defeat him.

Goku has grown considerably more powerful ever since he met Beerus, but defeating a God of Destruction is something unheard of. Beerus is literally the embodiment of destruction thanks to his divine powers paired with eons of experience, making it virtually impossible for any mortal to overpower him.

Although Whis was initially believed to be Beerus' attendant , it turns out he's an Angel and the martial arts teacher of the God of Destruction. Angels exist to guide and supervise the Gods of Destruction, placing them on a completely different tier of power even among the immortal beings. Whis is the one who taught Goku to tap into the power of Ultra Instinct that only Angels have been able to use for eons, considering that it requires the user to be in a state of mind and self-movement where the body reacts autonomously to danger without requiring conscious thought from the brain.

Angels like Whis are always in a state of Ultra Instinct, as evidenced by their white hair. Not only that, but Ultra Instinct is so difficult to master that even Beerus can only use it imperfectly. On top of his extraordinary godly abilities that canonically make him more powerful than Beerus, Whis has the ability to turn three minutes into the past and easily travel between universes with a speed that no one can match.

Frieza is one enemy Goku hasn't been able to get rid of no matter how many times they fight. Starting from the Namek Saga, the villain keeps returning with new powers even after his death. Whether his army revived him or if Goku needed his help, regardless of the situation, the villain remains a crucial part of Dragon Ball Super since the beginning. After the Tournament of Power between all universes was over, he came back to life and dedicated himself to training again.

He returned at the end of the Granolah the Survivor Saga and showed off his new form, which he named Black Frieza. Unlike Golden Frieza, this new form is unimaginably more powerful and better in terms of speed and durability. He managed to defeat Goku in his Ultra Instinct state and Ultra Ego Vegeta together in one blow. The impact of the attack forced them both out of their transformations, displaying the difference in their skills.

Out of all the villains in Dragon Ball Super , Zamasu gave Goku and the others the most difficulty. He altered timelines, stole Goku's body, ruined the world of Future Trunks, and even made himself undefeatable. As a Kai, he was already immortal with an endless lifespan, but that doesn't mean he couldn't be killed. This is why he used the Super Dragon Balls to make himself an absolute immortal and teamed up with his future self to destroy all mortals from the universe. Fused Zamasu especially was the most powerful form he had since it's a fusion of Black Goku and his future self.

With the abilities of a Saiyan and the immortality of a God, Fused Zamasu possessed the level of power that even Beerus couldn't overcome. Although in terms of raw power, Beerus would stand on top, even he couldn't do anything to stop him. Goku had no choice but to use Omni-King Zeno's help to erase the timeline and Zamasu with it.

While he may look like a mascot character, Grand Zeno, the Omni-King, is the most feared being by everyone in all universes. This goes for even the Gods of Destruction, who are always careful in his presence. Zeno may not be a fighter, but he is the most powerful being in all Universes as someone who holds absolute authority and the power to erase entire timelines in an instant. This divine being doesn't possess any martial arts ability, so he is unable to track the high-speed movements of fighters.

However, he doesn't need to fight anyone in order to destroy them. Just one thought of Zeno can erase Goku's existence along with his universe, which is why it worked out best for the Saiyan to befriend this godly being instead of making an enemy out of him. Without Zeno's interference, there was no way for anyone to stop Zamasu's rampage.

Which of these Dragon Ball Super characters do you think poses the biggest challenge for Goku, and is there anyone else he cannot defeat at his current level? Share your picks in the comments below!

I’ve been watching it since the beginning, when audiences were first introduced to Enid Turner, an ambitious woman serving as Bertha Russell’s lady’s maid.

In Season 2 of The Gilded Age , Enid seemed to have finally caught a break, marrying Joshua Winterton for financial security and a more prominent place in society.
